issues.display_title: Issue #36: Make Enfuse (Auto Stitching) Tool Free — Remove From Paywall
issues.main_description_html:
Source

User feedback

Problem / Request

The Enfuse (Auto Stitching) tool is currently gated behind the paywall (Pro-only). Product decision: remove Enfuse from the paywall so it is available to all users for free.

This is a gating/entitlement change only — not a request to reimplement Enfuse.

Scope

  • Remove the Pro/subscription gate from the Enfuse (Auto Stitching) feature.
  • Ensure free-tier users can access and run Enfuse without any trial/Pro prompt or upsell modal.
  • Leave the Enfuse functionality itself unchanged.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Enfuse (Auto Stitching) is fully usable by free-tier (non-subscribed) users.
  2. No paywall / "Pro feature" / trial modal is shown when accessing Enfuse.
  3. Other Pro-gated features remain gated (only Enfuse is ungated).

issues.display_title: Issue #61: Preview: Allow Zoom (And Pan) on Flat Images Mode
issues.main_description_html:
Source

User feedback

Problem

In Preview, the Flat view mode does not allow zooming into the image. Users need to zoom in to inspect detail on flat (non-360-projected) images.

Request

Enable zoom on Flat images in the Preview viewer (zoom in/out + pan), the same way users expect to inspect image detail.

Scope

  • Add zoom (and pan while zoomed) to the Flat view mode in Preview.
  • Support common zoom interactions: scroll/pinch to zoom, and drag to pan when zoomed in.
  • Keep existing Preview controls (view-mode toggles, navigation) working.
  • Confirm interaction does not conflict with the pan/hand tool already present.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Users can zoom into a Flat image in Preview (in and out).
  2. While zoomed, users can pan around the image.
  3. Zoom is smooth and does not break other Preview controls or view modes.

issues.display_title: Issue #72: Fix Issue Manual Leveling Output is Severely Distorted and Does Not Match UI Preview
issues.main_description_html:
Description

A critical issue has been reported in the Manual Leveling tool (GoThru Photo Studio v1.1.4). When a user adjusts the Roll, Pitch, and Yaw sliders, the horizon appears correctly leveled within the tool's live preview canvas. However, after applying the changes, the resulting equirectangular output image is severely distorted with an exaggerated, curved horizon.

User Notes:

  • The live preview inside the Manual Leveling tool correctly reflects the intended adjustments.
  • The final processed image does not match the preview at all.
  • Auto-leveling is functioning correctly, but users cannot rely on it for every image, making manual leveling a blocker for their workflow.

Source: user feedback (albug, Slack) — "the manual leveling does not work properly. this is what I set … and this is what I get. auto leveling seems to be OK but auto level does not work for all of them." (Screenshots: correct in-tool preview vs. distorted final output.)

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Open an uneven 360 image in the application.
  2. Navigate to the Manual Leveling tool.
  3. Adjust the Roll, Pitch, and Yaw sliders to straighten the horizon in the preview (e.g., Yaw: -110.4).
  4. Click Apply to process the image.
  5. Open the resulting image in the main Preview viewer.
  6. Observe that the horizon is highly distorted/curved rather than straight.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. The mathematical transformation applied to the final image perfectly matches the WebGL preview shown in the UI.
  2. Users can manually adjust Roll, Pitch, and Yaw, and the resulting saved image maintains a straight, correct horizon.

PASSED FROM TESTER

issues.display_title: Issue #66: Handle Issue "Edit" Button Routes to Last Active Tool Instead of Main Tools Edit Dashboard
issues.main_description_html:
A UX/routing issue has been reported in GoThru Photo Studio (v1.1.4). When a user clicks the "Edit" button in the top navigation bar, the application remembers their previous state and routes them directly back into the last specific tool they had open (e.g., Image Minifier or AI Nadir Patching).

The expected behavior is that the "Edit" button should act as a hard reset for that section. Clicking it should always land the user on the main Tools Dashboard (the grid view displaying all available editing tools), regardless of what tool they were using previously.

Source: user feedback (albug, Slack) — "There is a problem with the Edit button, it takes me the last tool I had open. It should always take me to see all the Tools." Annotated screenshot shows the Edit button should land on the Tools grid, not inside a tool.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Clicking the "Edit" button from anywhere in the app (File Manager, Preview, etc.) always opens the main Tools grid showing all available tools.
  2. Clicking the "Edit" button while actively inside a specific editing tool safely unmounts that tool and returns the user to the main Tools grid.
  3. The routing change does not cause data loss if a user accidentally navigates away while processing an image (ensure standard unmount warnings still apply if a job is running).

🧪 Testing Scenario (for QA)

Feature: "Edit" button in the top navigation bar
Goal: Verify the Edit button always resets to the main Tools grid, never re-opening the last tool.

Pre-conditions

  • App running (v1.1.4+), a folder with images opened.

Test 1 — Edit reopens Tools grid (not last tool)

  1. Click Edit → open a specific tool (e.g. Image Minifier).
  2. Navigate away: click File Manager (or Preview).
  3. Click Edit again.
  • ✅ Expected: Lands on the main Tools grid (all tools visible).
  • ❌ Fail: Reopens Image Minifier (or whatever tool was last used).

Test 2 — Edit while inside a tool

  1. Open Edit → AI Nadir Patching (or any tool).
  2. While inside that tool, click Edit in the top nav again.
  • ✅ Expected: The tool unmounts cleanly and the main Tools grid is shown; no leftover tool UI/state.

Test 3 — From every entry point

  1. From File Manager, click Edit → Tools grid shown.
  2. From Preview, click Edit → Tools grid shown.
  3. After using a tool then returning, click Edit → Tools grid shown.
  • ✅ Expected: Every path lands on the Tools grid.

Test 4 — No data loss while a job is running

  1. Open a tool and start processing an image (job running).
  2. Click Edit in the top nav to navigate away.
  • ✅ Expected: Standard unmount/leave warning appears (per existing behavior); confirming does not corrupt or silently drop the running job; cancelling keeps the user in the tool.

Regression checks

  • Other nav buttons (Preview, File Manager, Upload) still work.
  • Selecting a tool from the grid still opens it normally.
  • Repeating Edit → tool → Edit multiple times stays consistent (no sticky state).

DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-07-17.at.10.17.44.mov

QA Validation - 31 August 2026

Field Value
Scope Top-navigation Edit routing reset
Environment GoThru Photo Studio desktop app; real-device validation supplied by QA tester
Overall result Passed
Evidence source QA tester-confirmed real desktop run; source review performed locally

Acceptance Test Results

ID Scenario Expected Result
TC-01 File Manager to Edit after opening a tool Main Tools grid, not the last active tool Passed
TC-02 Preview to Edit after opening a tool Main Tools grid, not the last active tool Passed
TC-03 Edit while already inside a tool Active tool unmounts and the main Tools grid is shown Passed
TC-04 Repeat Edit to tool to Edit No sticky tool state across repeated navigation Passed
TC-05 Edit during active image processing Processing continues and completes without data loss Passed
Regression Preview, File Manager, Edit dashboard, and tool entry remain usable No regression observed Passed

Test Methods

Method Coverage Result
White box switchToEdit() clears editMenu; Edit.tsx renders <Menu /> when it is null Passed
Gray box Real desktop navigation plus processing-state observation Passed
Black box Repeated navigation from File Manager, Preview, and an active tool Passed
Confusion matrix Not applicable: this is deterministic navigation/state behavior, not a classifier N/A

Code Review

src/renderer/components/layouts/Header/hooks/useViewerSwitch.ts switchToEdit() clears editMenu both when entering Edit and when Edit is already active. Passed
src/renderer/components/features/Edit/Edit.tsx A null editMenu deterministically renders the main Tools Dashboard (<Menu />). Passed

Processing Navigation Observation

No leave-warning dialog was displayed when Edit was clicked during processing. The real desktop run confirmed that processing continued and completed successfully, with no observed data loss. This satisfies the issue's data-preservation outcome.

issues.display_title: Issue #60: MultiView: Stack 360 Images Vertically (One on top of the other), Not Side by Side
issues.main_description_html:
Source

User feedback

Problem

In MultiView / compare mode, 360 (equirectangular/panorama) images are arranged side by side (horizontally). Because 360 images are wide (2:1), a side-by-side layout makes each one small and hard to inspect.

Request

For 360 images, stack the views vertically — one on top of the other — instead of side by side. This gives each wide panorama more horizontal room and matches how 360 content is best compared.

Scope

  • In MultiView, change the layout so 360 images stack vertically (rows) rather than horizontally (columns).
  • Applies specifically to 360/panorama images (confirm behavior for non-360/flat images — likely keep as-is).
  • Preserve existing MultiView features (up to 8 views, sync, per-tile controls).

Acceptance Criteria

  1. When comparing 360 images in MultiView, tiles are stacked vertically (one above the other), not side by side.
  2. Each 360 image gets full available width, improving visibility.
  3. MultiView still supports its existing max count and controls.

DEMO BY DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-07-17.at.15.55.04.mov

QA Validation - 31 August 2026

Field Value
Scope MultiView layout for 360/equirectangular images
Environment GoThru Photo Studio desktop app v1.1.10 on Windows
Test data Two real JPEG equirectangular panoramas: 8000x4000 each
Overall result Failed - coding bug confirmed

Acceptance Test Results

ID Scenario Expected Actual Result
TC-01 Select two 360 images in MultiView Tiles stack vertically; each receives full available width Both tiles render side by side in the same row Failed
TC-02 Verify layout geometry Same left position and increasing top position Tile 1: x=400, y=381; Tile 2: x=1162, y=381 Failed
TC-03 Existing MultiView controls Max-count and Column controls remain available MultiView Max. 9 and Column control remain visible Passed

Test Methods

Method Coverage Result
White box Reviewed useFlatMode.ts and FlatModeContent.tsx layout path Failed
Gray box Installed desktop app rendered two real 8000x4000 equirectangular files Failed
Black box Confirmed the 360 case does not receive a distinct vertical layout Failed
Confusion matrix Not applicable: this is deterministic UI layout behavior, not a classifier N/A

Code Review

Area Finding
src/renderer/features/preview/hooks/useFlatMode.ts getColumnCount() always returns a horizontal grid-cols-* layout; it has no panorama-specific vertical branch.
src/renderer/features/preview/FlatModeContent.tsx MultiView always applies grid ... ${getColumnCount()} and does not choose vertical rows for 360 images.
Runtime result The rendered grid class was grid-cols-2; both 8000x4000 panorama tiles had the same top coordinate and different left coordinates.

Coding Bug

MultiView does not distinguish 360/equirectangular images from flat images when choosing its grid direction. It therefore violates the required vertical stacking and reduces the horizontal viewing area for wide panoramas.

Evidence

Screenshot - real desktop MultiView with two 8000x4000 panoramas rendered side by side:

Video - real desktop recording with GoThru navbar visible:

issue-60-real-app-multiview.mp4

QA Verdict

Failed. Fix the MultiView layout branch so equirectangular/panorama selections use a single vertical column while flat-image MultiView behavior remains unchanged.
